name: Graph Neural Network
description: Neural architecture that reasons over graph-structured data through iterative message passing between nodes. Learns relational patterns in molecules, social networks, and knowledge graphs. Mirrors the relational nature of this ontology itself — intelligence as connection.

core_attributes.architecture: message-passing neural network on graph topology
core_attributes.learning_mode: supervised and self-supervised on graph structure

training_paradigm: message-passing iterations with graph-level loss functions

scope.definition: Node classification accuracy advantage of message-passing GNNs over MLP baselines without graph structure, on standard citation network benchmarks (Cora, Citeseer, PubMed).

evidence.source: Kipf & Welling (2017) 'Semi-supervised classification with graph convolutional networks', ICLR; Gilmer et al. (2017) 'Neural message passing for quantum chemistry', ICML.
cross_domain_examples: GCN on Cora: 81.5% vs MLP 55.1% — 26.4 point accuracy gain from graph structure exploitation
molecular property prediction: MPNN achieves 0.91 MAE reduction on QM9 vs MLP baseline
belief propagation in probabilistic graphical models: formal message-passing analogue with convergence guarantees

scope.falsifiability: If GNN performance on Cora drops to within 5% of MLP when node features are shuffled (destroying graph-feature correlation), the message-passing benefit depends on graph-feature alignment, not structure alone.
scope.measurement_limits: Message-passing depth is limited by over-smoothing — beyond 4-6 layers, node representations converge and accuracy degrades. Long-range dependencies require graph transformers rather than standard GNNs.

scope.definition: Graph-level classification accuracy of hierarchical graph pooling operators vs global mean pooling on molecule classification benchmarks — measured as AUC improvement on PROTEINS and MUTAG datasets.

evidence.source: Ying et al. (2018) 'Hierarchical graph representation learning with differentiable pooling', NeurIPS; Bianchi et al. (2020) 'Spectral clustering with graph neural networks', NeurIPS.
cross_domain_examples: DiffPool hierarchical pooling: +4-7% AUC vs global mean pooling on graph classification benchmarks
pooling preserves local structure (cliques, bridges) lost by global mean — hierarchical information retention
convolutional neural net pooling: analogous spatial hierarchy compression for image classification

scope.falsifiability: If global mean pooling achieves statistically equivalent graph classification accuracy to hierarchical pooling across 10+ standard benchmarks, hierarchical structure provides no additional discriminative information.
scope.measurement_limits: Pooling benefit depends on whether graph structure is discriminative for the task. For graphs with homogeneous structure, pooling provides marginal benefit. Benefit is larger on graphs with clear hierarchical community structure.
